newsitem.title: GERMANY: Focus - Schwarz Pharma eyes strong 97 growth after Q1 data.
newsitem.headline: Focus - Schwarz Pharma eyes strong 97 growth after Q1 data.

text.p: German drugs group Schwarz Pharma AG on Wednesday forecast higher profits and sales for the whole year after posting a 9.2 percent jump in first quarter 1997 pre-tax profits.

"We expect to post a five percent rise in 1997 sales and a continuing increase in profits," management board chairman Patrick Schwarz-Schuette said, predicting the group's earnings per share should jump at least nine percent to 4.90 marks.
Despite the outlook however, shares fell over six percent in post-bourse trading as dealers worried about increased competition in some of the group's key product areas.
The family-owned pharmaceuticals group, which had been a market favourite since its bourse debut two years ago, said it planned to grow further with takeovers and by concentrating its sales abroad.
"In order to increase our position in key markets, we will continue to keep our eyes open for acquisitions and cooperations," Schwarz-Schuette said.
Last year Schwarz Pharma's foreign turnover topped domestic sales for the first time ever, surging 26 percent to 610.8 million marks.

Almost half of foreign sales, 269.3 million marks, or one quarter of total turnover, came from the U.S., where Schwarz Pharma has expanded aggressively, entering a number of strategic alliances last year.
The company had already announced a 17.5 percent rise in total 1996 turnover to 1.19 billion marks.
Net profit climbed 14.4 percent to 103.8 million marks and the company confirmed that it would raise its dividend payout by 20 percent to 1.50 marks.
The group said that cost-cuttings, acquisitions and internal growth were jointly responsible for results.
The group's return on capital stood at 24.8 percent, down from last year's 26.2 percent and return on sales stood at 8.7 percent after 8.9 percent in 1995.

In light of the sheer size of the U.S. market and the fact that new drugs are often approved more quickly there, Schwarz-Schuette said "in the U.S. and many other nations the opportunity for profits are much greater."

Like many of its competitors, Schwarz Pharma said foreign sales would continue to fuel growth, particularly as the German government clamps down further on spending, giving physicians an annual budget for prescription drugs.
This year Schwarz Pharma plans to launch Edex, a product designed to treat erectile dysfunction, in the U.S. and in Germany and launch high blood pressure treatments in Germany, Italy and the U.S.
Despite the optimistic outlook, shares in the group ended the bourse session down over two percent at 130 marks and fell another 4.6 percent in after hours trading to 124.95 marks.

Dealers linked the losses both to disappointment that the group had pared its sales forecast to five percent from a six to eight percent rise forecast earlier this year and sharper competition in some of its products in Germany.
Analysts however were unavailable for more detailed comment as the company was still holding its analysts meeting.
